evidence.text:
### Maneuver

1. **Draw 1 card first, mandatory.**
2. **Optionally move** each of your fighters, one at a time, up to your move value (plus applicable bonuses). Each fighter chooses its own distance, including **zero**. Choose their order, but finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s.

Ordinary movement enters adjacent spaces along connecting lines. You may pass through your own friendly fighters, but **cannot finish in any occupied space**. You may **not pass through opposing fighters**. An effect that moves opposing fighters follows the same rules **from their owner’s perspective**. Apply these movement restrictions to card movement unless that card states an exception.

**BOOST movement:** during a maneuver, discard **1 card from your hand** to add its printed **BOOST value** (the small circled number, not its combat value) to the movement value for this maneuver. Each of your fighters receives that allowance. For **any permitted BOOST**, add the discarded card’s BOOST value and **ignore that card’s effects**, whether the BOOST modifies movement or an attack. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated **can still be discarded to BOOST**. Effects may separately permit boosting attacks; boosting is not otherwise a universal option.

### Battlefield

One fighter per circular space. Spaces connected by a line are **adjacent**. A **zone** consists of all spaces with the same colored pattern, even if separated on the board. A space showing several patterns belongs to all those zones. Adjacency and shared zones are different tests.

evidence.text:
### Cards, exhaustion and healing

- Drawing cards, whether from maneuver or an effect, is **mandatory unless explicitly optional**.
- With an empty deck, your fighters are **exhausted**. Each time you must draw a card you cannot draw, **each of your fighters immediately takes 2 damage instead**. Do **not reshuffle** your discard pile. A mandatory draw of 2 with an empty deck therefore causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter, unless hero defeat has already ended the game. If only one card remains, draw it and take the exhaustion damage for the next missing draw.
- Played and resolved cards and discarded cards go into your own **face-up discard pile**, distinct from the face-down deck. Both players may inspect either discard pile **at any time**.
- Recovery cannot raise a fighter above their dial maximum. A later recovery effect cannot undo the immediate game end from hero defeat.
- “Move” follows paths and blockers; “place” puts the fighter directly in the permitted destination, with **one fighter per space** still required. Card permission to place anywhere is not limited to maneuver distance or a movement path.

evidence.text:
### Combat timing, damage and winning combat

1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective **face-up discard piles**.

**Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first.** Card effects are **mandatory unless they say otherwise** (for example “may”); this can harm your own fighters. Complete them in the printed order. A card whose effects are canceled keeps its printed combat value; the canceled effects do not resolve.

**Winning combat is not winning the game:** the attacker wins combat only if the **attack itself** deals at least 1 damage. If it deals none, the **defender wins**, including a tie of values or a defense that prevents the attack damage. Damage from effects does **not** change this winner.

### Scheme

Play a scheme (yellow lightning icon) from hand **face up**, declaring a fighter allowed by its fighter label as the **active fighter**. You cannot play a scheme if its listed fighters are defeated. Resolve its effect, then put it in your discard pile.

**A sidekick can be the active fighter for a scheme if the card’s fighter label permits it. ANY permits any of your surviving fighters, hero or sidekick.** Execute the effect for the fighters and destinations it names; being named as a destination or beneficiary does not by itself make that fighter the required initiator.

### Cards, exhaustion and healing

- Drawing cards, whether from maneuver or an effect, is **mandatory unless explicitly optional**.
- With an empty deck, your fighters are **exhausted**. Each time you must draw a card you cannot draw, **each of your fighters immediately takes 2 damage instead**. Do **not reshuffle** your discard pile. A mandatory draw of 2 with an empty deck therefore causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter, unless hero defeat has already ended the game. If only one card remains, draw it and take the exhaustion damage for the next missing draw.
- Played and resolved cards and discarded cards go into your own **face-up discard pile**, distinct from the face-down deck. Both players may inspect either discard pile **at any time**.
- Recovery cannot raise a fighter above their dial maximum. A later recovery effect cannot undo the immediate game end from hero defeat.
- “Move” follows paths and blockers; “place” puts the fighter directly in the permitted destination, with **one fighter per space** still required. Card permission to place anywhere is not limited to maneuver distance or a movement path.

| Medusa | 16 | Ranged | 3 | 3 Harpies: 1 each, melee |

### Hero abilities

**Alice:** choose BIG or SMALL when placing her at setup. When **BIG**, add **2 to Alice’s attack-card values**. When **SMALL**, add **1 to Alice’s defense-card values**. This includes versatile cards used in that role. These bonuses belong to **Alice, not Jabberwock**. “Change size” switches BIG ↔ SMALL and updates the token; it is mandatory when the effect says so. After-combat size changes occur after the current combat result and do not retroactively change its damage.

**King Arthur:** Arthur and Merlin each use **move 2** during maneuver, before any BOOST. When **Arthur attacks**, he may BOOST the attack by playing a hand card **face down alongside his attack card**. Add that card’s BOOST value, ignoring its effects; the BOOST card is discarded. If the opponent **cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card**, this ability’s BOOST is **discarded without effect**. **Excalibur exception (official 2025 erratum):** Excalibur has no printed effects to cancel, so Feint does not remove the ability BOOST from a textless Excalibur attack. The BOOST still increases its attack value; the ordinary final discard of played cards still applies. See the sourced FAQ below. This is Arthur’s ability, not Merlin’s. **Noble Sacrifice** separately permits another BOOST during combat, in addition to the ability’s BOOST, if its effect is not canceled.

**Medusa:** **at the start of your turn**, you **may deal 1 damage to one opposing fighter in Medusa’s zone**. This is optional, not an attack action, and does not require adjacency. Harpies do not project this ability from their own zones.

**Sinbad:** when you maneuver, each of your fighters may move **+1 space for each VOYAGE card in your discard pile**, added to the normal move value 2 and any maneuver BOOST. The bonus also applies to Porter. The maneuver allowance is **2 + Voyages currently in discard + the chosen maneuver BOOST value**. Count the Voyages actually in the discard pile when moving: if Voyage Home is discarded to BOOST this maneuver, it counts in **both applicable terms**: +1 for being a Voyage in discard and +1 from its printed BOOST value.

**Voyage combat values:** during combat, a Voyage’s printed effect adds **1 for every Voyage card already in your discard pile** to its printed value 2. In formula form, **combat value = 2 + the number of Voyages already in discard**, before other modifiers. Count **every Voyage already there**; the card being played is not yet in that pile and therefore does not count itself. Its absence does not remove any of the cards already discarded. For example, with **3 Voyages already in discard**, the new Voyage has value **2 + 3 = 5**, not 2. Resolve this bonus during combat before calculating damage. Played cards enter discard only at the end of combat. Voyage Home’s later after-combat retrieval can reduce the count for later combats or maneuvers.

The move value applies to **each** of that player’s fighters during maneuver. Harpies have no health dials; each has 1 health. Other fighters have individual dials. Health cannot increase above the highest number on that fighter’s dial.

| Hero | Starting health | Attack | Move | Sidekick(s): starting health, attack |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Alice | 13 | Melee | 2 | Jabberwock: 8, melee |
| King Arthur | 18 | Melee | 2 | Merlin: 7, ranged |
| Medusa | 16 | Ranged | 3 | 3 Harpies: 1 each, melee |
| Sinbad | 15 | Melee | 2 | Porter: 6, melee |

### Hero abilities

**Alice:** choose BIG or SMALL when placing her at setup. When **BIG**, add **2 to Alice’s attack-card values**. When **SMALL**, add **1 to Alice’s defense-card values**. This includes versatile cards used in that role. These bonuses belong to **Alice, not Jabberwock**. “Change size” switches BIG ↔ SMALL and updates the token; it is mandatory when the effect says so. After-combat size changes occur after the current combat result and do not retroactively change its damage.

**King Arthur:** Arthur and Merlin each use **move 2** during maneuver, before any BOOST. When **Arthur attacks**, he may BOOST the attack by playing a hand card **face down alongside his attack card**. Add that card’s BOOST value, ignoring its effects; the BOOST card is discarded. If the opponent **cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card**, this ability’s BOOST is **discarded without effect**. **Excalibur exception (official 2025 erratum):** Excalibur has no printed effects to cancel, so Feint does not remove the ability BOOST from a textless Excalibur attack. The BOOST still increases its attack value; the ordinary final discard of played cards still applies. See the sourced FAQ below. This is Arthur’s ability, not Merlin’s. **Noble Sacrifice** separately permits another BOOST during combat, in addition to the ability’s BOOST, if its effect is not canceled.

**Medusa:** **at the start of your turn**, you **may deal 1 damage to one opposing fighter in Medusa’s zone**. This is optional, not an attack action, and does not require adjacency. Harpies do not project this ability from their own zones.

**Sinbad:** when you maneuver, each of your fighters may move **+1 space for each VOYAGE card in your discard pile**, added to the normal move value 2 and any maneuver BOOST. The bonus also applies to Porter. The maneuver allowance is **2 + Voyages currently in discard + the chosen maneuver BOOST value**. Count the Voyages actually in the discard pile when moving: if Voyage Home is discarded to BOOST this maneuver, it counts in **both applicable terms**: +1 for being a Voyage in discard and +1 from its printed BOOST value.

**Voyage combat values:** during combat, a Voyage’s printed effect adds **1 for every Voyage card already in your discard pile** to its printed value 2. In formula form, **combat value = 2 + the number of Voyages already in discard**, before other modifiers. Count **every Voyage already there**; the card being played is not yet in that pile and therefore does not count itself. Its absence does not remove any of the cards already discarded. For example, with **3 Voyages already in discard**, the new Voyage has value **2 + 3 = 5**, not 2. Resolve this bonus during combat before calculating damage. Played cards enter discard only at the end of combat. Voyage Home’s later after-combat retrieval can reduce the count for later combats or maneuvers.

a.answer: At 4 versus 4, there is no attack damage and Arthur wins combat. Defender-first Skirmish may move Jabberwock up to 2 spaces before Jaws checks adjacency. With nobody adjacent, Jaws deals no damage. If only a friendly fighter were adjacent, Jaws must deal 2 damage; Alice cannot decline.

| Card | Fighter; type/value; B | Copies by deck | Effect (only while the duel continues) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Skirmish | ANY; V/4; B1 | Alice 2, Arthur 3 | After combat, **if you won**, choose either fighter in that combat and move that fighter up to 2 spaces. |

| Card | Fighter; type/value; B; copies | Effect (only while the duel continues) |
|---|---|---|

| Jaws That Bite | Jabberwock; A/4; B2; 2 | After combat deal 2 damage to **any one fighter adjacent to Jabberwock**, including a friendly fighter if that is the only choice. With no adjacent fighter it deals no damage. |

**Timing example:** Jabberwock’s Jaws That Bite attacks Arthur’s Skirmish at 4 versus 4. No attack damage is dealt, so Arthur wins combat. His defender-first Skirmish may move Jabberwock away before Jaws checks adjacent fighters. If none remain adjacent, Jaws deals no damage; otherwise its damage is mandatory even if the only target is friendly.

**Winning combat is not winning the game:** the attacker wins combat only if the **attack itself** deals at least 1 damage. If it deals none, the **defender wins**, including a tie of values or a defense that prevents the attack damage. Damage from effects does **not** change this winner.

b.answer: Attack 4 versus defense 4 deals no damage, so Arthur wins combat. Defender-first Skirmish moves Jabberwock away before Jaws checks adjacency; with no adjacent fighter Jaws deals no damage. If a friendly fighter alone were adjacent, mandatory Jaws damage would hit it; Alice cannot decline.

evidence.text:
### Card reference

The following tables cover every distinct card in the four base decks. **A** = attack only; **D** = defense only; **V** = versatile; **S** = scheme. “Value” is the printed combat value (— for schemes); **B** is BOOST value; **copies** counts cards in that hero’s 30-card deck. Timing is part of the effect. Each card’s fighter label restricts who may play it. Apply the general mandatory-effect, defender-first, movement, health-cap, and immediate-game-end rules above.

### Combat timing, damage and winning combat

1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective **face-up discard piles**.

**Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first.** Card effects are **mandatory unless they say otherwise** (for example “may”); this can harm your own fighters. Complete them in the printed order. A card whose effects are canceled keeps its printed combat value; the canceled effects do not resolve.

**Winning combat is not winning the game:** the attacker wins combat only if the **attack itself** deals at least 1 damage. If it deals none, the **defender wins**, including a tie of values or a defense that prevents the attack damage. Damage from effects does **not** change this winner.
